guide_enrichment.narrative:
We see Wake Forest’s opener as encouraging context, not proof that the offense will translate against Miami. Wake Forest produced 559 yards, Gio Lopez threw for 350 yards and three touchdowns without an interception, and the offensive line allowed no sacks. Still, our efficiency numbers give Miami the advantage against both the pass and the run, with the clearest concern coming when Wake Forest tries to create scoring opportunities.

The more interesting part is Wake Forest’s explosiveness. It generated four plays of at least 30 yards against Akron, giving the offense a plausible way to shorten drives and create variance. But those bursts came in one game, and our longer-run view is considerably more favorable toward Miami’s pass defense than Wake Forest’s passing offense. Because our expectation is effectively aligned with the market, we do not see enough disagreement at the current price to justify a position.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Lopez and Wake Forest’s downfield passing game against Miami’s pass defense. Lopez’s debut included a 78-yard touchdown to Carlos Hernandez, while Hernandez finished with 165 receiving yards. Those explosive connections matter because Wake Forest may need chunk gains rather than consistently efficient drives against a defense our numbers rate well.

For us, the question is whether Wake Forest can produce enough of those plays without relying on an outlier rate. If Miami limits the explosives and forces longer possessions, the matchup tilts toward the defensive advantage reflected in our numbers.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest opened the 2026 season with a 38-16 victory over Akron on Sept. 3.
Wake Forest produced 559 total yards against Akron, including 356 passing yards and 203 rushing yards.
Wake Forest converted 7 of 15 third downs and both of its fourth-down attempts against Akron.
Wake Forest committed no turnovers and recovered one Akron fumble in the season opener.

quarterback.fact: Gio Lopez started his Wake Forest debut against Akron and completed 21 of 32 passes for 350 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions while adding 39 rushing yards.
Lopez's 78-yard touchdown pass to Carlos Hernandez against Akron was the longest completion of Lopez's collegiate career.
Lopez transferred to Wake Forest from North Carolina after starting 11 games there in 2025 and completing 65.1 percent of his passes for 1,747 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions.
Before North Carolina, Lopez played at South Alabama under current Wake Forest offensive coordinator Rob Ezell.
Wake Forest's unofficial projected depth chart lists redshirt freshman Steele Pizzella as the backup to Lopez.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running back Ty Clark III rushed seven times for a career-high 105 yards against Akron, including a career-best 57-yard run.
Wide receiver Carlos Hernandez caught five passes for 165 yards and a touchdown against Akron and added 18 punt-return yards.
Hernandez recorded a career-high 148 yards after the catch against Akron.
Over his last five games, Hernandez has averaged 107.6 receiving yards, caught at least five passes in every game and scored five receiving touchdowns.
Antonio Meeks had 93 receiving yards against Akron, including a 72-yard reception.
Wide receiver Ny Carr joined Wake Forest after previously playing at Miami.
Center Will Way joined Wake Forest from Weber State in January 2026 and was selected as a team captain.

Wake Forest's unofficial projected offensive line consists of Tolu Olajide at left tackle, Clinton Richard at left guard, Will Way at center, Ryan Berger at right guard and Aidan Martin at right tackle.

defensive_personnel.fact: Linebacker Aiden Hall, defensive lineman Langston Hardy and defensive back Davaughn Patterson were selected as 2026 team captains.
Hall became a starter in 2025 and finished that season with 73 tackles, eight tackles for loss and three passes defended.
Wake Forest's unofficial projected defensive front lists Langston Hardy and Gabe Kirschke at end, Dallas Afalava at defensive tackle and Zach Lohavichan at nose guard.

The unofficial projected secondary lists Deuce Blades II and Ashaad Williams at cornerback, Rushaun Tongue at free safety, Davaughn Patterson at strong safety and Braylon Johnson at the Star position.
Joshua Patterson joined Wake Forest after playing four games with two starts at Iowa State in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Jake Dickert is in his second season as Wake Forest head coach after being hired on Dec. 18, 2024.
Rob Ezell is Wake Forest's offensive coordinator, and Dan Enos serves as co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
Scottie Hazelton is the defensive coordinator, and Freddie Banks is the co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.
Dyrell Roberts became Wake Forest's wide receivers coach in 2026 after coaching East Carolina's receivers from 2023 through 2025.

offensive_context.fact: Wake Forest allowed no sacks in its 2026 opener against Akron.
Wake Forest's 2025 offensive line allowed 17 sacks after allowing 42 in 2024.
Wake Forest generated four plays of at least 30 yards against Akron: touchdown passes of 78 and 72 yards, a 57-yard run by Ty Clark III and a 31-yard reception by Antonio Meeks.
Wake Forest averaged more than 28 points per game and produced 27 plays of at least 30 yards during the 2025 season.

defensive_context.fact: Wake Forest held Akron to 305 total yards, including 149 rushing yards and 156 passing yards.
Wake Forest recorded seven tackles for loss and two sacks against Akron.
Akron converted 6 of 14 third downs and scored on all three of its red-zone trips.
Wake Forest held seven of 13 opponents to 14 points or fewer in 2025 and did not allow a touchdown in consecutive ACC games against Virginia and North Carolina.

special_teams.fact: Kicker Connor Calvert made three of four field-goal attempts against Akron and scored 12 points.
Wake Forest averaged 22.0 yards per punt return and posted a 49.0-yard net punting average in the opener.
The unofficial projected depth chart lists Carlos Hernandez as the primary punt returner, Koredell Bartley as the primary kickoff returner and freshman Ethan Hyams as the punter.
